title: Words that sound alike
goal: Two words cannot share a stroke. Spelling picks different vowels first; if they still collide, the star breaks the tie.

blocks.x: Rule 1: the spelling picks the vowel
Many sound-alikes differ in how they are spelled, and the dictionary writes that difference into the vowel. If you can see the word, you can pick the stroke.
Rule 2: the star breaks the tie

Some pairs have the same spelling pattern, so the vowel cannot help. Usually the commoner word keeps the plain stroke. The other gets a star, in a fixed ladder: plain, star on the first stroke, star on the last stroke, then extra star strokes.
The spelling also matters at the start of a word. `wr` takes [[WR]] and `wh` takes [[WH]], so [[right|ROEUT]] and [[write|WREU]] and [[rite|RAOEUT]] are three different strokes.
You never choose between two strokes for one word. The word has one primary. When a sound-alike pair exists, **read the word's spelling** and the right stroke follows.

blocks.q: Which is *sail*, as in a boat?
blocks.why: `ai` is the long vowel `AEU`; the silent-e spelling is the shorter `AE`.
